The paper acknowledges "We have not tested above 4B" and the end-to-end conversion uses a fixed µ=3, leaving higher-µ (closer-to-bf16) full-model claims empirically unvalidated, making the title claim an extrapolation beyond what is demonstrated.

evidence.claim: The title and abstract overstate the generalizability of the method, claiming accuracy approaching any quantization level and arbitrarily close to bf16, but the empirical results only validate model-level performance up to ~5.7 effective BPW.
evidence.excerpt: The title and abstract claim the method offers "Accuracy Approaching Any Quantization Level" and "approaches bf16 accuracy arbitrarily closely". While Corollary 1 (Appendix A) mathematically proves this for isolated matrix approximation, the empirical results only validate model-level performance up to ~5.7 effective BPW on a 4B parameter model. Extrapolating matrix-level limits to full-model end-to-end scaling without empirical validation constitutes an unsupported generalization.

judge_panel.reason: The paper's theoretical convergence claim in Corollary 1 applies to individual matrix approximation, but the full-model empirical validation only covers up to ~5.7 effective BPW on a 4B model. The paper acknowledges "We have not tested above 4B" and the end-to-end conversion uses a fixed µ=3, leaving higher-µ (closer-to-bf16) full-model claims empirically unvalidated, making the title claim an extrapolation beyond what is demonstrated.

The abstract/title are broad (e.g., "Ternary LLM PTQ with Accuracy Approaching Any Quantization Level" and "ExTernD approaches bf16 accuracy arbitrarily closely"), but the abstract also grounds this in a matrix-level proof: "We prove the residual decreases monotonically in k and can be driven below any ε > 0." At the same time, the paper concedes "end-to-end task accuracy is not yet measured," so whether the framing overgeneralizes from matrix reconstruction to full-model accuracy is unclear.

The title claims "Accuracy Approaching Any Quantization Level", but the abstract and Section 3.5 confirm that the end-to-end model evaluation is only tested up to "a full Qwen3.5-4B conversion at µ = 3 ... at ~5.7 effective bpw", making the reviewer's point about lack of empirical validation for higher levels valid.
